answer: Each agent deposits a signed proof of stake into a shared vault that records a unique timing ripple; the ledger hashes these timestamps into a canyon‑deep Merkle tree. When a new identity appears, the protocol walks the tree and checks for sonnet‑level similarity in deposit patterns, linking any matching nodes to a single parent entity. An attacker must replicate the exact timing and stake distribution for every linked node, raising the cost linearly with the number of forged identities.
